blocks.text: The Encoding Techniques module completed the work of turning every categorical feature into something a model can actually use. Handling Imbalanced Data addresses a genuinely different, equally common real world challenge, one that has nothing to do with how features are encoded, what happens when the target class itself is genuinely rare, fraud detection, rare disease diagnosis, and equipment failure prediction all genuinely share this exact same problem.

This topic, the first in this new module, covers what class imbalance genuinely means, how under sampling addresses it by genuinely removing rows from the majority class, the real, permanent information loss that removal causes, the difference between random and smarter, more deliberate removal strategies, and the specific, real situations where under sampling genuinely makes sense as a first choice.
1. What Class Imbalance Genuinely Means
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443277173-159683657.png

A genuinely imbalanced target class means one class, the majority, genuinely dominates the dataset, while the other, the minority, appears in only a genuinely small fraction of rows. Fraud detection is a classic real example, genuinely fraudulent transactions might make up less than 5 percent of an entire dataset, with legitimate transactions filling the rest.

This matters genuinely a great deal for training, a model can often achieve a genuinely high overall accuracy simply by predicting the majority class every single time, while completely failing to identify the minority class that usually matters most in a real, practical sense.
2. How Under Sampling Actually Works
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443277173-84860017.png

Under sampling genuinely removes rows from the majority class until its count becomes comparable to the minority class, rather than trying to add more minority examples. A dataset with 950 majority rows and 50 minority rows might genuinely become 50 and 50, after removing 900 majority rows entirely.
This is genuinely the most direct way to address imbalance, the resulting dataset genuinely has a balanced class distribution a model can train on without automatically favoring the majority class.
3. A Worked Example
Applying random under sampling with the imbalanced-learn library shows this direct removal in action, on a small, deliberately imbalanced dataset.

code.content:
from imblearn.under_sampling import RandomUnderSampler
import pandas as pd

X = pd.DataFrame({"amount": [50, 60, 45, 5000, 30, 70, 40, 6200]})
y = pd.Series([0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1])

sampler = RandomUnderSampler(random_state=42)
X_resampled, y_resampled = sampler.fit_resample(X, y)

print(y_resampled.value_counts())

blocks.text: The genuinely majority class, originally 6 rows against only 2 minority rows, gets reduced down to match the minority class count exactly, producing a genuinely balanced 2 and 2 split ready for training.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: Always apply under sampling only to the training set, never to validation or test. Evaluating on an artificially balanced test set would genuinely misrepresent how the model performs on real, naturally imbalanced data.

blocks.text: 4. The Real, Permanent Cost: Information Loss

blocks.alt: The Real, Permanent Cost: Information Loss
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443277174-826330177.png

Every majority class row that gets removed is genuinely discarded entirely, along with whatever real, useful signal it might have carried about the majority class actual patterns. In a genuinely large dataset, removing 900 out of 950 majority rows throws away the genuine vast majority of what the model could have learned about that class.

This creates a genuine, real risk of underfitting the majority class specifically, a model trained on too few majority examples might genuinely fail to learn its real patterns well, even while successfully balancing its exposure to the minority class.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: Under sampling genuinely, permanently discards real data. This cost is worth weighing directly against the alternative approaches covered in the rest of this module before committing to it.

blocks.text: 5. Random Versus Smarter Removal Strategies
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443277174-746483859.png

Random under sampling genuinely removes majority rows arbitrarily, with no regard for which specific rows might matter more than others. Smarter variants, like Tomek links or NearMiss, genuinely target rows near the decision boundary specifically, the region where majority and minority examples sit closest together and genuinely matter most for a model to learn the real distinction correctly.

These smarter techniques attempt to minimize the real information loss covered above, by removing the majority rows that are genuinely least useful, redundant examples far from the boundary, rather than removing rows at random and potentially discarding genuinely valuable ones.

blocks.text: 6. When Under Sampling Genuinely Fits
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443277174-871348584.png

Under sampling genuinely makes the most sense when the majority class is so large that losing a significant portion of it is a genuinely acceptable tradeoff, a dataset with millions of majority rows can often afford to lose most of them and still retain a genuinely representative sample. It also matters when genuinely faster training on a smaller resulting dataset is itself a real, practical goal.

For a genuinely smaller dataset, though, where the majority class itself is not overwhelmingly large, under sampling real information loss becomes a much more serious concern, and the alternative techniques covered later in this module become genuinely more attractive.

blocks.text: 7. The Class Balance Before and After

blocks.alt: The Class Balance Before and After
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443277175-232489152.png

Visualizing the genuine before and after class counts makes the real transformation this technique performs directly concrete, a dataset that started genuinely dominated by one class ends up genuinely balanced, at the direct, real cost of discarding the majority class rows that no longer fit within that new, smaller count.
This balance is genuinely the entire point, a model trained on this resulting, balanced dataset no longer has a built in numeric incentive to simply favor the majority class by default.
8. Under Sampling Versus What Comes Next

blocks.alt: Under Sampling Versus What Comes Next
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443277517-685111081.png

Under sampling addresses imbalance by genuinely shrinking the majority class down, at the real cost of permanently losing data. The next topic takes the genuinely opposite approach entirely, growing the minority class instead, keeping every majority row intact.

Over Sampling, covered next, duplicates minority class examples until the classes reach a genuine, comparable balance, avoiding the information loss covered in this topic, but introducing its own, different real risk instead.

items: Class imbalance means one class genuinely dominates the dataset while the other appears only rarely.
Under sampling genuinely removes majority class rows until both classes reach a comparable count.
This genuinely, permanently discards real majority class data and its potential signal.
Random removal is arbitrary; smarter variants like Tomek links target the decision boundary specifically.
Under sampling fits best with a genuinely huge majority class that can afford real data loss.
The next topic, Over Sampling, takes the genuine opposite approach, duplicating minority rows instead of removing majority ones.
